hypotheses.claim: The council median reduces precipitation error versus the average individual model.
hypotheses.update: Keep council median as the default headline.

hypotheses.claim: Higher model disagreement predicts larger forecast error after normalizing for rainfall magnitude.
hypotheses.effect: normalized corr 0.13 · high/low normalized error 1.04× · heavy-rain corr −0.27
hypotheses.update: Keep disagreement visible, but do not turn it into a confidence penalty yet.

hypotheses.claim: Forecast skill materially degrades from 1 to 3 to 5 days.
hypotheses.update: Make forecast horizon a first-class confidence input.

hypotheses.claim: The council median remains useful on heavy-rain days.
hypotheses.update: Keep the council as the main heavy-rain summary.

hypotheses.claim: COMMONS should lower confidence when disagreement is high and lead time is long.
hypotheses.effect: horizon is supported; disagreement penalty is not
hypotheses.update: Confidence v0.2 = source health + empirically measured horizon skill. Show disagreement separately.

limitations: ERA5 is reanalysis, not a local rain gauge.
Point precipitation is not basin-integrated precipitation.
This tests precipitation forecast skill, not human flood impact.
Operational model versions change over time.
603 samples are not 603 independent events; dates and locations are correlated.
